item.text: {"answer":"227","solution":"Let N(d) count triples with d dividing a,b,c and satisfying the sum and congruence. Since d|60, scaling by d gives x+y+z=60/d and x+2y+3z≡0 (mod 7); as d is invertible modulo 7, the congruence is preserved. For n=60/d, the number F(n) of nonnegative solutions with x+y+z=n and x+2y+3z≡0 (mod 7) is (1/7)∑_{j=0}^6∑_{x+y+z=n}ω^{j(x+2y+3z)}. The j=0 term is binom(n+2,2). For j≠0, the inner sum is the coefficient of t^n in 1/((1-ω^j t)(1-ω^{2j}t)(1-ω^{3j}t)); summing over j=1,…,6, or grouping terms by residues modulo 7, gives F(60)=265, F(30)=68, F(20)=33, F(12)=16, F(10)=11, F(6)=6, F(5)=5, F(4)=3, F(3)=2, F(2)=1, F(1)=1. Möbius inversion on divisors of 60 therefore gives the primitive count ∑_{d|60}μ(d)F(60/d)=265−68−33−11−5+6+3+1−1=227.","insight":"For any triple with sum 60, its common gcd divides 60.","insight_justification":"If g divides a,b,c, it divides their sum a+b+c=60; hence only divisors of 60 need to be considered in Möbius inversion."}
